faq.question: What is the DAC in CJC-1295?
faq.answer: DAC stands for Drug Affinity Complex — a maleimidopropionyl linker that covalently binds to Cys³⁴ of serum albumin. This conjugation extends half-life from minutes to ~8 days by preventing renal clearance and enzymatic degradation.

faq.question: Difference between CJC-1295 with DAC and without DAC?
faq.answer: With DAC: ~8 day half-life → sustained GHRH activation → chronic GH/IGF-1. Without DAC: ~30 min half-life → discrete GH pulse → mimics endogenous pulsatile secretion. Choice depends on research objective.

faq.question: Why pair CJC-1295 with Ipamorelin?
faq.answer: CJC-1295 amplifies the GHRH signal (the 'on' switch). Ipamorelin suppresses somatostatin tone (the 'off' switch). Together they produce a larger net GH pulse than either alone — well-characterized synergism.

faq.question: How should CJC-1295 (DAC) be stored?
faq.answer: Lyophilized: 2–8°C, desiccated, 24-month stability. After reconstitution, store at 2–8°C. The DAC-albumin conjugate forms spontaneously — this is expected and part of the molecule's designed mechanism.

faq.question: What configurations are available?
faq.answer: Standard: 2mg × 10 vials. Bulk: 5mg × 10 vials. Custom mg/vial for OEM/private-label. CJC-1295 (no DAC) also available as a separate SKU for pulsatile GH protocols.
